title: A healthy social life and, where possible, a healthy and sustainable diet: how the social and material environments shape eating practices
abstract: Purpose Grounded in social practice theory, this study aims to describe the coordination of the eating practices of a socially diverse sample of individuals, half of whom have shifted toward healthier and more sustainable diets, while the other half have not. Design/methodology/approach Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 32 individuals. Through reflexive thematic analysis, the authors examine informants’ eating practices to understand how social and material environments facilitate or hinder the adoption of healthier diets. Findings The authors’ findings indicate that changes in eating practices are shaped by coordination, asymmetric negotiation and a sense of belonging. The fragility of plant-based practices does not primarily stem from weak commitment but from a lack of infrastructural support. Individuals revert to dominant eating practices not because they lack knowledge, awareness or moral concern, but because the social and material environment privileges asymmetric coordination. Eating is fundamentally a practice of social integration. Consequently, maintaining a healthy social life frequently takes precedence over maintaining dietary consistency. Sustainable transitions will therefore succeed only when environmentally aligned practices become socially effortless, when they allow individuals to preserve belonging without friction. Pra…
venue: Qualitative Market Research: An International Journal

title: Supplier development and buyer’s relative relationship value – a dyadic examination in an emerging market
abstract: Purpose Fierce competition in many industries has prompted buying firms to participate in supplier development by sharing information (SDI) and by improving suppliers’ capabilities (SDC). Building upon transaction cost theory and social exchange theory, this study aims to examine the double-sided effects of SDI and SDC on buyer’s relative relationship value (BRVA), which measures the value buyers perceive from the relationship relative to that suppliers perceive. Design/methodology/approach The analysis is based on questionnaires received from managers of 110 matched dyads of buying and supplying firms in Vietnam. Findings The study finds that SDI exhibits a positive but decreasing returns-to-scale effect on BRVA, while SDC follows a U-shaped pattern. Moreover, the solidarity norm moderates these relationships in distinct ways. Practical implications The results imply that buying firms should be cautious about their investments in SDI and SDC because their effects on BRVA are nonlinear and contingent on relational governance conditions. Originality/value This paper introduces BRVA as a dyadic perspective for assessing the nonlinear outcomes of different supplier development investments on both buying and supplying firms.

title: Civil partnerships in Zimbabwe: The church’s response
abstract: Zimbabwe’s Marriages Act harmonises previously fragmented legal systems governing different marriages into a single-statute framework. This codification improves legal certainty and facilitates practical engagement for family law practitioners and litigants alike. Going beyond simple harmonisation of existing marital classifications, the Act introduces civil partnerships as a unique legal marital category. The religious approval of this legislation by the Zimbabwean churches remains contested, reflecting a range of doctrinal views across different denominations. In Zimbabwe’s predominantly Christian society, supported by constitutional guarantees of religious freedom, the positions of church organisations merit careful consideration. Churches advocating for monogamous marriage, mainly Mainline Protestant and Pentecostal groups, view civil partnerships as morally questionable. Conversely, the White Garment Apostolic churches adopt a different theological stance that accommodates polygamous marriage practices. It is concluded that forbidding civil partnerships for individuals already in monogamous civil unions would help maintain a clear divide between monogamous relationships and polygamous arrangements. Further, the article suggests revising the Marriages Act to include only unregistered civil marriages within the scope of civil partnerships. A document-based qualitative resear…

title: Research on the Mechanism by Which Lysophosphatidylcholine Regulates the Inflammatory Response in Ischemic Stroke Through the NF-κB Signaling Pathway
abstract: Background: Neuroinflammation following ischemic stroke is a significant factor leading to secondary brain damage, but the role of lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) in this process remains unclear. This study sought to determine whether LPC participates in the post-ischemic inflammatory process and to evaluate if this effect is mediated through the nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway.Methods: For the in vivo study, male C57BL/6 mice aged 8–10 weeks were randomly assigned to a sham group (n = 10) and a middle cerebral artery occlusion model group (MCAO, n = 10). The suture occlusion method was applied to induce MCAO, with 60 min of ischemia followed by 24 h of reperfusion. LPC concentrations in serum and brain tissue were measured using ELISA. The protein levels of tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), interleukin-1β (IL-1β), and interleukin-6 (IL-6) in cerebral tissue, together with the expression of nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) pathway-associated proteins (p-p65, p65), were evaluated using ELISA and Western blotting. TTC staining was performed to determine infarct size, while neurological deficits were scored with the modified neurological severity score (mNSS). For the in vitro study, BV2 microglial cells were subjected to oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) and allocated to four groups: Control, OGD, OGD+LPC, and OGD+LPC+BAY 11-7082. title: Global Demand‑And‑Value‑Driven Hype Cycles of Capitalism: A Socio‑Philosophical Analysis
abstract: Drawing on the authors’ definitions of the phenomenon of human natural needs and the phenomenon of val-ues, the article reveals the logic behind the successive reproduction of three global demand‑and‑value‑driven hype cycles of capitalism: the consumer cycle, the credit cycle, and the investment cycle. The instrumental and media function of the phenomena of pleasure, luxury, and success in launching and intensifying the corre-sponding cycles is identified. The possibility of two modifications of the representation of these phenomena in the public consciousness – the demand‑based and the value‑based – is substantiated. It is shown how the transformation of these phenomena from one modification to another, carried out by the marketing strategy of capitalism, contributes to the intensification of demand‑and‑value hype cycles. In connection with the under-standing of labor in Karl Marx’s social philosophy as an object‑transforming activity, the article identifies the logic of the transformation of the phenomenon of pleasure in the context of capitalism – from a phenomenon accompanying the satisfaction of needs and performing a signaling function into an independent need. The logic of the functioning of luxury as a means of legitimizing capitalist elites is disclosed through and analysis of the spiritual foundations of capitalism in the studies of Max Weber and Thorstein Veblen.

title: CmHSFA3-CmBRC1a-CmHB40 module inhibits axillary bud development in response to high temperature
abstract: Abstract Branching is a key determinant of plant architecture, directly influencing growth, yield, and resource allocation. High temperature (HT) inhibits plant growth and development, often leading to alterations in plant architecture. However, the molecular mechanisms underlying temperature-induced inhibition of branching remain elusive. Here, we discovered that CmBRC1a is strongly induced by HT and inhibits axillary bud development in chrysanthemum. We further demonstrated that the heat shock transcription factor CmHSFA3 directly activates CmBRC1a by binding to its promoter, thus acting as its upstream regulator. Overexpression of CmHSFA3 further confirmed its role in suppressing branching. The finding that HT cannot completely suppress the enhanced branching phenotype of CmBRC1a knockdown lines suggests that HT-regulated branching is not entirely dependent on CmBRC1a. Similar to previously reported BRC1-mediated pathways, CmBRC1a directly activates the expression of CmHB40, thereby increasing abscisic acid (ABA) accumulation, which ultimately inhibits shoot branching. Our findings reveal CmHSFA3-CmBRC1a-CmHB40 module inhibits axillary bud development in response to HT, providing new insights into how environmental cues shape plant architecture.

title: Dynamic response of pile driven by different impact energies in clay–mudstone layers: field understanding based on fiber optic sensing
Phygital Art as a Response to the Crisis of NFT Art: A Culturological Analysis of Transforming Digital Art Practices
abstract: The article presents a culturological analysis of phygital art as a possible structural response to the multilevel crisis of NFT art. The relevance of the research is driven by the need to re-evaluate phygital practices, the de-velopment of which slowed down amidst the collapse of the crypto art market. The author identifies the key reasons for the NFT model crash: the speculative nature of the art market, the dematerialization of the artistic experience, institutional inadequacy, and the “inflation of novelty”. The study substantiates the hypothesis, which suggests that phygital art, thanks to the organic synthesis of digital and physical dimensions, is capable to overcome these conceptual expenses. Particular attention is paid to the capacity of phygital art for institution-al rootedness and the purchasing strata unification – the young audience of the digital era and traditional col-lectors. It is concluded that phygital art represents a dialectical overcoming of the limitations of both purely ana-log and virtual art in tune, acting as a promising paradigm for the development of artistic culture in the post-digital era.

title: Extending Erikson’s generativity to leadership: a psychobiographical study
abstract: Purpose Erikson’s concept of generativity has shaped developmental psychology for over seven decades, yet its application within management and leadership scholarship remains narrow, Western-centric and largely interpersonal in focus. This paper aims to trace that theoretical gap and argues that generativity, properly reframed, constitutes a foundational and undertheorized dimension of leadership. Design/methodology/approach A psychobiographical research design is used, applying Erikson’s psychosocial theory to the life and leadership of Sabu M. Jacob, founder of Kitex Garments and the Twenty20 Kizhakkambalam civic initiative in Kerala, India. Drawing exclusively on triangulated secondary sources, the analysis traces three successive developmental resolutions (industry, identity and generativity) across Jacob’s lifespan. Findings Generativity, in this context, is not a private virtue but an institutionally expressed, culturally embedded leadership orientation. Jacob’s developmental trajectory demonstrates how early resolutions of competence and identity accumulate into a form of leadership that bridges entrepreneurial success, employee welfare and civic transformation. Three theoretical propositions are advanced linking generativity to authentic, servant and transformational leadership traditions. Research limitations/implications As a single-case psychobiography relying on sec…

title: Enhancement of performance by the utilization of one-dimensional OCDMA codes in a three-dimensional system
abstract: Abstract The present research evaluates a new approach to solve problems associated with temporal spreading, spectral spreading, and spatial mode allocation of the OCDMA network. The new system uses the DEU code for temporal spreading, the MS code extension for spectral spreading, and MD code for spatial mode allocation. The system utilizes a modified DEU code for temporal spreading, the modified MS code extension for spectral spreading, and MD code for spatial mode allocation. The encoder in this system generates codes in the spectral, temporal spreading, and spatial domains. There are noises taken into consideration for the analysis of the proposed OCDMA implementation: phase-induced intensity noise, thermal noise, and shot noise. Results show that the new 3D OCDMA system outperforms current codes in terms of transmission rate, user count, required spectral width, and received power. The suggested 3D DEU-MS-MD ( M = 7, N = 20, P = 7) code enables data transmission for up to 300 users. It achieves a BER of 10 −10 at −10 dB m received power. However, the 3D DEU-DEU-MD code supports only 220 users, while the 3D-MD and 2D-MS codes support 240 and 128 users, respectively.

title: Minimum-Disclosure Civil-Military Deconfliction for UAS Traffic Management in Thailand: A Simulation Study
abstract: Background: Unmanned aircraft system traffic management (UTM) depends on information exchange for conflict management, yet civil-military coordination creates tension between safety visibility and operational security. Objective: This study develops and evaluates a trusted minimum-disclosure broker that computes on protected civil and military intent while releasing only a time-limited conflict token and safe-action advisory. Methods: A reproducible Monte Carlo experiment compared no cross-domain sharing, five-second delayed state sharing, full trajectory sharing, and the minimum-disclosure broker across three civil traffic densities, three service-latency levels, three navigation-error levels, and 250 replications per condition. Results: Across 27,000 policy evaluations, 72,446 encounter events generated 17,029 modeled conflicts before intervention. The broker left 2.60% unresolved (95% cluster-bootstrap interval: 2.36%–2.86%), compared with 2.43% for full sharing, 15.80% for delayed sharing, and 37.49% for no sharing. Its paired difference from full sharing was 0.17 percentage points (95% interval: −0.13 to 0.49), satisfying a one-percentage-point engineering noninferiority margin while exposing no raw military trajectory states to the civil domain. Conclusion: The findings support staged evaluation of a Thai UTM architecture in which safety decisions are shared but sensitive…
venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology

title: The Expanding Role of Carbohydrate Antigen 125 in Heart Failure: From Tumour Marker to a Cornerstone of Heart Failure Management. An Updated Narrative Review
abstract: Congestion is central to heart failure (HF) but remains difficult to quantify. Carbohydrate antigen 125 (CA125), also known as mucin 16, released by mesothelial cells, captures two pathways relevant to HF: fluid overload and inflammation. This narrative review summarises biological mechanisms and clinical applications. Across acute and chronic settings, CA125 tracks systemic and right-sided congestion, complements natriuretic peptides and shows lower dependence on renal function. Higher levels identify patients at risk for death and readmission; in ambulatory HF with reduced ejection fraction it predicts events, while in HF with preserved ejection fraction its signal is strongest in congestion-dominant phenotypes. Serial testing mirrors decongestion and clinical course; CA125-guided care has reduced rehospitalisations and improved renal function measures in selected populations. Advantages, wide availability, standardisation and low cost, support use in practice. Key gaps include phenotype-specific threshold, sampling interval and integration into actionable algorithms. Overall, CA125 has moved from tumour marker to practical tool that refines congestion assessment, improves risk stratification and informs individualised therapy in contemporary HF care.

title: The forgotten core of the father of strategic management: revisiting the Ansoff–Mintzberg debate and the strategic success hypothesis
abstract: Purpose This study aims to revisit the Ansoff and Mintzberg exchange as a contingency-based debate about the conditions under which planning and emergent strategy are valid. It argues that the debate’s lasting significance lies in the question of strategic correctness and repositions Ansoff’s Strategic Success Hypothesis (SSH) as a central but unevenly consolidated contribution to strategy theory. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a historiographic and conceptual analysis anchored in Ansoff’s (1991) critique of the design school debate and his contextualization of emergent strategy within bounded environmental conditions. It traces how SSH, defined as the alignment among environmental turbulence, strategic aggressiveness and capability responsiveness, was unevenly operationalized and tested and connects this lineage to contemporary research on industry norms, benchmarking and strategic posture. Findings The study finds that Ansoff’s response to Mintzberg reframes emergent strategy as context dependent by distinguishing incremental from discontinuous turbulence, while also showing that SSH remained influential but empirically fragmented because validation efforts did not consolidate into a visible research program. It further suggests that contemporary benchmarking and strategic posture research reopen this unresolved issue by explaining movement relative to norms w…

title: Talent Management and Innovation Capacity as Determinants of the Economic Performance of Creative Entrepreneurs Based on Local Wisdom
abstract: The creative economy is a sector that relies on creativity, knowledge, skills, and innovation to generate economic value. The sustained performance of creative business operators depends not only on the ability to produce unique products but also on the capacity to manage talent and develop innovation capabilities to respond to changes in the business environment. This study aims to analyze the influence of talent management and innovation capacity on the economic performance of creative business operators rooted in local wisdom. A quantitative approach with an explanatory design was employed. Data were collected via questionnaires distributed to 100 creative business operators using a five-point Likert scale. Talent management was measured using eight indicators, innovation capacity using six indicators, and economic performance using five indicators. The data were analyzed using the Partial Least Squares-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) approach. The analysis results indicate that talent management has a positive and significant effect on economic performance (β = 0.322; t = 3.790; p < 0.001). Innovation capacity also has a positive and significant effect on economic performance (β = 0.444; t = 5.225; p < 0.001). An R² value of 0.416 indicates that talent management and innovation capacity explain 41.6% of the variation in economic performance. The findings confirm that…

Effect of R&D innovation cooperation on corporate innovation: the mediating role of digital transformation capability
abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital economy, service firms face increasing pressure to adopt open innovation frameworks that actively leverage external knowledge. This study investigates the impact of Research and Development (R&D) Innovation Cooperation on Corporate Innovation within service enterprises, focusing on the structural mediating role of Digital Transformation Capability. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View (RBV), Dynamic Capability Theory, and Open Innovation Theory, a research model was developed and tested using Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). The empirical findings reveal that R&D innovation cooperation serves as a powerful antecedent that significantly enhances a firm’s digital transformation capability. Furthermore, this newly developed digital capability exerts a positive direct effect on corporate innovation by enabling data-driven decision-making and operational flexibility. Crucially, the results demonstrate that digital transformation capability plays a vital mediating role in the relationship between R&D cooperation and corporate innovation. This underscores that external knowledge acquired through collaboration yields substantial innovative performance only when successfully integrated into the firm’s internal digital dynamic processes. By explicating the inner mechanism of transforming external alliances into internal digital capabilities, this resear…

title: Rethinking conceptually distinct but empirically intertwined constructs in work motivation
abstract: Purpose Job autonomy, intrinsic motivation and job satisfaction are typically treated as conceptually distinct constructs linked through causal or mediational relationships, yet survey-based studies consistently report strong empirical proximity among them even when they meet or approach conventional discriminant-validity standards. This conceptual paper asks what such structural relationships represent when conceptually distinct constructs are strongly intercorrelated in self-report models. Design/methodology/approach The paper develops an interpretive representation perspective treating self-reported motivation constructs as cognitively co-organized articulations of work experience. Survey data from 349 working adults serve an illustrative function, with each respondent providing ratings under two framings of their work experience (on-site and work-from-home) and partial least squares structural equation modeling examining within-person reweighting of structural configurations. Findings Autonomy, intrinsic motivation, and job satisfaction are generally psychometrically distinguishable yet structurally intertwined, with the closest construct pairings approaching conventional discriminant-validity thresholds. Differences across the two framings appear as selective reweighting of structural associations rather than uniform moderation or stable causal ordering, a pattern consiste…

title: Rural women as place-makers through informal waste collection in QwaQwa, South Africa
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the livelihood approaches, socio-economic effects and challenges related to informal waste collection, focusing on informal women waste collectors in rural QwaQwa, South Africa. It addresses gaps in gender and rural–urban divides by positioning these women as active place-makers who, through their daily practices, transform marginalised rural spaces into cleaner, more functional and resilient environments. This spatial agency supports household survival, inclusive rural development, and reduced vulnerability while advancing circular economy principles. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in the sustainable livelihood framework (SLF) and place-making theory, the study adopted a qualitative case study design. Data were collected through focus group discussions, interviews, field observations and secondary sources and analysed thematically. Findings Informal waste collection serves as a vital livelihood strategy for women in rural QwaQwa, driven by poverty and unemployment. Leveraging social networks, local knowledge and child collaboration, these women generate income and contribute to sustainable waste management. Critically, their everyday practices of waste recovery actively reshape rural landscapes, reducing illegal dumping, improving public spaces and fostering environmental stewardship, positioning them as unrecognised place-makers. title: The impact of digital technologies, intellectual capital, and corporate social responsibility on firm performance
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to explores the effects of digital technologies (DT), intellectual capital (IC) and corporate social responsibility (CSR) on firm performance (FP). It further examines the moderating role of IC in driving the link between DT, CSR and firm performance. Design/methodology/approach Using a cross-sectional data set of 14,597 observations, the Generalized Method of Moments (GMM) is used to address potential endogeneity. DT is treated as an endogenous variable and instrumented with regional variables and proxies for workforce composition. Findings The findings show that DT and IC enhance firm performance, while CSR reduces it. Moreover, IC positively moderates the relationship between CSR and firm performance, while it negatively moderates the relationship between DT and firm performance, suggesting potential misalignment between existing IC and DT. Originality/value This research integrates the resource-based view (RBV), dynamic capabilities theory (DCT) and stakeholder theory (ST) to develop a theoretical framework to understand how DT, IC and CSR jointly affect firm performance. It also extends the literature by exploring the moderating effects of IC on performance through DT and CSR, which have been overlooked.
venue: VINE Journal of Information and Knowledge Management Systems

title: Examining organizational performance through hard and soft models of HRM: evidence from knowledge-intensive organizations
abstract: Purpose Based on the social exchange theory and resource-based view, this study aims to examine the relationship between hard human resource management (HRM) practices (job description, performance appraisal, downsizing and outsourcing, and work hours and intensification) and organizational performance, as well as between soft HRM practices (training and development, employee involvement and participation, communication and work–life balance) and organizational performance. Design/methodology/approach A questionnaire survey was conducted among 338 human resource (HR) managers of different information technology companies in India. The sample was selected based on a stratified random sampling method. Hierarchical component modeling was conducted for hard HRM practices, soft HRM practices and organizational performance. Partial least squares structural equation modeling was used to evaluate the model and hypotheses of the study. Findings The findings indicate that training and development, employee involvement and participation, communication and Work–life balance positively influence organizational performance, demonstrating a significant effect. Moreover, job description, downsizing and outsourcing and work hours and intensification significantly influence organizational performance. Among soft HRM practices, communication exhibits the strongest relationship, highlighting its c…

title: Does gender influence career choices? Empirical evidence from business administration students in the Philippines
abstract: This study examined whether gender is associated with career choice motivations among business administration students in the Philippines. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data were collected from 446 students (94 males, 352 females) at Mindanao State University-Iligan Institute of Technology through a validated 20-item survey measuring intrinsic, extrinsic, institutional, and interpersonal factors. Independent-samples t-tests revealed statistically significant gender differences in intrinsic factors (t[444] = -1.976, p = 0.049, d = -0.21), extrinsic factors (t[444] = -2.818, p = 0.005, d = -0.29), and interpersonal factors (t[444] = 2.595, p = 0.010, d = 0.29), while institutional factors showed no significant difference (t[444] = -1.031, p = 0.303). Female students reported higher intrinsic and extrinsic motivation scores, whereas male students scored higher on interpersonal factors. Effect sizes were small, indicating that the differences, while statistically significant, do not represent large practical disparities. These findings suggest that gender-responsive career development programs that capitalize on intrinsic and extrinsic motivations for female students, and that strengthen interpersonal networking for male students, are warranted. The results contribute to career development research in Southeast Asian higher education and carry context-specific implic…

title: Understanding food quality labels in complex markets. The role of heuristics in consumer decision-making
abstract: Purpose This study examines how consumers interpret differentiated food quality labels in complex markets, focusing on cognitive accessibility and heuristics to explain why signals such as local origin can outweigh formal or technically complex certifications. Design/methodology/approach The article combines bibliometric analysis with a qualitative scoping review. A corpus of 510 publications from 1996–2026 was analysed using science-mapping techniques, followed by a cluster-guided synthesis of evidence on label proliferation, consumer interpretation, willingness to pay and territorial outcomes. Findings The literature has shifted from information provision and attitudes towards the economic valuation of sustainability attributes. The synthesis identifies label overload, attention competition, cue substitution, hypothetical bias and divergence between consumer valuation and territorial outcomes. Local origin often functions as an accessible cue bundling authenticity, trust, freshness and community support, which can increase its influence relative to more complex certifications. Practical implications Regulators, certification bodies and firms should assess overlap before adding labels, organise information hierarchically and combine credible verification with intuitive design. Consumer education should clarify what accessible claims such as “local” do and do not guarantee. Ori…

title: Threats to the economic security of industrial enterprises
abstract: The article examines approaches to the identification and classification of threats to the economic security of industrial enterprises. The analysis of existing interpretations of the concepts "factor", "threat" and "risk" of economic security in the scientific literature is carried out, their essential differences and cause-and-effect relationships are established. The authors systematize the classification features of threats by the environment of occurrence (external and internal), functional components (financial, personnel, technical and technological, informational, legal, environmental), levels of the economic system, nature of impact and time horizon of manifestation. Based on the generalization of theoretical approaches and taking into account the industry specifics of industrial enterprises, the authors propose a multidimensional typology of threats based on five classification criteria: by the nature of impact on the economic security system, by the degree of controllability on the part of the management subject, by the nature of the source of origin, by the time horizon of manifestation and implementation, by the possibility of prevention and minimization. The developed typology allows enterprises to improve the quality of threat identification, make informed choices of protection tools and effectively allocate resources between various areas of economic security.
venue: JOURNAL OF MONETARY ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT

title: The Influence of Islamic Leadership and Islamic Organizational Culture on Turnover Intention Mediated By Employee Engagement at Assalaam Foundation Bandung
abstract: The intention to change jobs threatens the sustainability of an organization; This study examines how Islamic Leadership and Islamic Organizational-Culture influence the intention to change jobs amongst teachers-staff at the Assalaam Foundation in Bandung, with Employee Engagement as a mediating variable. The researchers conducted a survey of 155 respondents; the questionnaire employed a five-point Likert-type scale, The PLS-SEM analysis revealed that out of five direct structural paths, only two paths are statistically significant: Islamic Leadership significantly enhances Employee Engagement (β = 0.586, p < 0.001), and Islamic Organizational Culture significantly drives Employee Engagement (β = 0.320, p = 0.009). Conversely, neither Islamic Leadership (β = -0.218, p = 0.288) nor Islamic Organizational Culture (β = -0.147, p = 0.458) exerts a statistically significant direct effect on Turnover Intention. Furthermore, Employee Engagement does not significantly influence Turnover Intention (β = 0.030, p = 0.850$) and fails to serve as a significant mediating variable for both Islamic Leadership (β = 0.017, p = 0.854) and Islamic Organizational Culture (β = 0.009, p = 0.859). Overall, the results of this study indicate Islamic leadership and organizational culture do enhance staff engagement but are not sufficient to reduce their desire to resign, either directly or through that …

title: A Load-Adaptive Virtual Resistance Strategy for Decentralized Control of Low-Voltage Islanded Microgrids
abstract: The voltage regulation of inverter-based islanded microgrids with virtual impedance frequently deteriorates under higher load demand due to voltage drops across the virtual impedance and the feeder. Conventional droop control with a fixed virtual resistance (Rv) improves current sharing by impedance matching but amplifies voltage sag as the load increases. This paper proposes a novel load-adaptive virtual resistance strategy for decentralized control of low-voltage microgrids. Unlike conventional fixed virtual resistance methods and many existing adaptive virtual impedance approaches, the proposed method directly embeds a prescribed voltage-regulation coefficient into the Rv formulation. The adaptive virtual resistance is analytically determined using the allowable voltage deviation, inverter rating, feeder resistance, and locally measured dq-axis voltage and current components. As the load demand increases, the calculated virtual resistance decreases automatically, thereby limiting the voltage drop introduced by the virtual resistance while preserving proportional power sharing among parallel inverters. The adaptive law is implemented in the dq reference frame using locally measured voltages and currents. A cascaded PI controller structure comprising an inner current loop and an outer voltage loop is used for control. Comprehensive tests under various load change scenarios are…

title: Unpacking the behavioural pathways to organisational resilience: gendered pathways of organisational citizenship behaviour linking transformational leadership and resilience
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how transformational leadership is translated into organisational resilience through organisational citizenship behaviour (OCB) and whether these behavioural pathways differ by gender among administrative officers in Sri Lankan state universities. It moves beyond leader-centric explanations by positioning employee behaviour as a mechanism through which leadership becomes an organisational capability. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted using a structured five-point Likert-scale questionnaire administered through Google Forms. A total of 250 questionnaires were distributed; 232 valid responses were obtained. Partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to test the hypothesised relationships and OCB mediation, with separate structural models used to examine gender-based pathways. Findings Transformational leadership had no significant direct effect on organisational resilience for either gender, while its indirect effect through OCB was significant, indicating full mediation. Gendered differences emerged in pathway strength: transformational leadership had a stronger effect on OCB among male officers than female officers, whereas OCB had a stronger effect on organisational resilience among female officers than male officers. Environmental dynamism strengthened the OCB–resilience relatio…

title: Influence Green Perceived Risk, Green Perceived Value, Green Word of Mouth to Green Purchase Intention in Con-sumers Indomaret in Joglo, West Jakarta
abstract: This study investigate the influence of green perceived risk, green perceived value, and green word of mouth on green purchase intention. This research employed a causal associative approach. The population of this study consisted of all consumers of Indomaret Point SPBU BP AKR in Joglo, West Jakarta. A total of 165 respondents were selected as the sample through the distribution of a google form questionnaire using a purposive sampling technique. Data analysis was conducted using the structural equation modeling (SEM) approach based of on partial least square (PLS) with SmartPLS 4.1 as the tools. The results of this study indicate that green perceived risk, green perceived value, and green word of mouth have significant effect on green purchase intention.
venue: International Journal of Economics, Management and Accounting

title: Worldview Security as a Factor of Protection under the Influence of Soft Power
abstract: The article is based on the author’s theoretical and methodological framework applied to the philosophical analysis of the phenomenon of worldview security. This framework relies on the organic theory of national se-curity developed by A.I. Melikhov, within which national security is interpreted not only as a state of protection of state institutions and territorial integrity, but also as the ability of society to self preserve (consolidation in the face of external and internal threats). The object of the study is the national security of the Russian Federation, its role and significance in the context of the use of cognitive warfare – soft power. The subject of the study is worldview security, and the phenomenon of this concept is examined in the context of countering the applica-tion of soft power. The relevance of this research lies in proposing a solution to the issue of adopting preventive measures to neutralize sources of tension arising from the informational impact on society by creating a buffer zone, which is represented by worldview security. The novelty consists in conducting a restorative procedure for the national security system, which is necessary to meet new standards. The work employs methods of social statics and social dynamics, as well as the analysis of social changes and transformations. The dialectical method was actively used, in particular the laws of…

title: Work-related learning in the AI era: the influence of formal and informal learning on employee attitudes toward artificial intelligence
abstract: Purpose Limited research has examined how employees’ broader participation in work-related learning relates to their attitudes toward artificial intelligence (AI). This study aims to examine how formal and informal work-related learning predicts positive and negative attitudes toward AI and whether these relationships differ across traditional, remote and hybrid work settings. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative, survey-based design was used to collect data from 252 full-time employees in the USA working in traditional, remote and hybrid settings. Relationships were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling, with multigroup analyses used to assess differences across work settings. Findings Formal work-related learning positively predicted both positive and negative attitudes toward AI. Informal work-related learning positively predicted positive attitudes toward AI, but was not significantly related to negative attitudes toward the technology. These relationships did not differ significantly across traditional, remote and hybrid work settings. Practical implications The findings demonstrate that employees’ broader engagement in work-related learning influences their perceptions of AI. Formal learning influences both favorable and unfavorable attitudes, which highlights the importance of developing employee capabilities while addressing concerns su…

title: Technological ecosystem mapping in facilities management: insights from patent data mining
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine the technological evolution of the facilities management (FM) sector through patent-based analysis, identifying innovation trajectories, leading countries and organizations and the primary thematic domains driving digital transformation. It also explores how intellectual property (IP) dynamics reflect technological maturity and competitiveness in FM. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative and exploratory design was used using FM-related patents (1977–2026) extracted from Google Patents and Lens.org. Advanced data mining, natural language processing (NLP), topic modeling and social network analysis were applied to map temporal trends, geographic distribution, technological clusters and collaboration networks among inventors and applicants. Findings Patent activity in FM has intensified since 2000, based on a data set of 2,967 patents, 3,018 inventors and 2,007 applicants. Topic modeling identified eight technological clusters structured around system architectures, operational control and digital infrastructure. Network analysis reveals sparse and fragmented collaboration patterns, with consistently high modularity (>0.97). The top applicants account for approximately 18% of patents, indicating moderate organizational concentration, whereas individual inventive activity remains highly dispersed. Geographically, innovation is concentrated…

title: Branding the green games: discursive power and communicative inequality in Olympic sponsorship narratives
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate how Olympic TOP sponsors construct green narratives across corporate, media and social media platforms and how these narratives contribute to communicative inequality in global environmental discourse. It explores the symbolic and rhetorical strategies used to project sustainability and interrogates the power structures that enable certain actors to dominate environmental meaning-making in the Olympic context. Design/methodology/approach This research uses a qualitative multimethod approach combining critical discourse analysis and qualitative content analysis. It analyses data from 10 Olympic TOP sponsors across environmental, social and governance (ESG) reports, news media and social media related to the Tokyo 2020, Beijing 2022 and Paris 2024 Olympic cycles, with focused data collection conducted between March 2023 and August 2024. Findings This study identifies three dominant greenwashing strategies – symbolic commitment, technological deflection and corporate social responsibility (CSR) performance theatre – varying across sectors. It highlights discursive patterns such as future deferral, selective framing and omission of dissent. Results show that corporate sponsors leverage symbolic alignment with the Olympics to shape sustainability discourse while excluding independent verification and marginalised voices, reinforcing communicati…

title: Analysis of the Motives for Working While Studying: A Case Study of Five Students at Megarezky University
abstract: This study analyzes the motives that encourage university students to work while studying, the strategies they employ to manage academic and employment responsibilities, and the perceived effects of working on their academic performance. The study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design involving five students at Megarezky University, Makassar, selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observation, and documentation, while data credibility was strengthened through source and methodological triangulation. The findings indicate that students' decisions to work while studying were primarily motivated by financial needs, the desire to reduce the economic burden on parents, the pursuit of financial independence, the productive use of available time, and the acquisition of work experience. To manage their dual responsibilities, students selected relatively flexible employment, established priorities, arranged work and study schedules, completed academic assignments according to planned schedules, and reduced non-essential activities. Working while studying generated both positive and negative consequences. Positive effects included additional income, greater financial independence, practical experience, and the development of responsibility. However, several students experienced fatigue, reduced study time, difficulty conce…
venue: International Journal of Science, Technology & Management

title: What internal characteristics could explain US wineries targeting upper-tier price segments?
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to examine how internal strategic and organizational characteristics are associated with upper-tier list-price positioning among US wineries, moving beyond accounts that focus mainly on terroir or regional reputation. Four directional hypotheses, derived from portfolio-focus, resource-based, signaling and cluster-theory perspectives, are tested. Design/methodology/approach This study analyses original survey data for 175 wineries in 25 US states. Respondents allocated production volume across four retail list-price bands (Value, Premium, Luxury and Iconic); upper-tier positioning is operationalized as a binary indicator equal to 1 when a volume-weighted price-band index exceeds the Premium/Luxury midpoint – equivalently, for nearly all wineries, when at least half of production volume lies at =$40 per 750 ml. Nested binary logits, an ordered logit and a mixed-effects ordered logit with a state random intercept are estimated, with the cutoff itself subjected to a systematic sensitivity analysis. Explanatory variables cover production scale, portfolio breadth, vertical integration, diversification, human and organizational capital, sustainability certification and regional location. Findings Upper-tier list-price positioning is more often reported by wineries that have operated longer, are organized as LLCs or corporations, source a higher share of grapes …
venue: International Journal of Wine Business Research

title: Multi-Scale Forecasting of Carbon Prices Using a Hybrid Deep Learning Model: Cross-Phase Validation on EU ETS
Characterization of spurious-electron signals in the double-phase argon TPC of the DarkSide-50 experiment
abstract: Abstract Spurious-electron signals in dual-phase noble-liquid time projection chambers have been observed in both xenon and argon Time Projection Chambers (TPCs). This paper presents the first comprehensive study of spurious electrons in argon, using data collected by the DarkSide-50 experiment at the INFN Laboratori Nazionali del Gran Sasso (LNGS). Understanding these events is a key factor in improving the sensitivity of low-mass dark matter searches exploiting ionization signals in dual-phase noble liquid TPCs. We find that a significant fraction of spurious-electron events, ranging from 30 to 70% across the experiment’s lifetime, are caused by electrons captured from impurities and later released with delay time constants on the orders of 5 ms and 50 ms. The rate of spurious-electron events is found to correlate with the operational condition of the purification system and the total event rate in the detector. Finally, we present evidence that multi-electron spurious electron events may originate from photo-ionization of the steel grid used to define the electric fields. These observations indicate the possibility of reduction of the background in future experiments and hint at possible spurious electron production mechanisms.

title: Narcissistic greenwashing: a cross-country evidence on the divergent paths to stock price crash risk
abstract: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to investigate the impact of greenwashing on stock price crash risk (SPCR) and to examine the context-dependent moderating effects of CEO narcissism and ownership structure across two distinct institutional settings, Indonesia and Singapore. Design/methodology/approach This study uses a composite environmental, social, and governance (ESG) score data set from London Stock Exchange Group and Bloomberg for the period of 2019–2024. The authors use panel data regression models to test the hypotheses. Findings The findings reveal a contextual divergence associated with executive personality. In Indonesia, CEO narcissism exacerbates the positive effect of greenwashing on SPCR. Conversely, in Singapore, CEO narcissism alleviates this risk. Research limitations/implications This study demonstrates that the psychological trait of CEO narcissism can provoke varying market reactions depending on the institutional environment. Stakeholders should consider both the CEO’s personality traits and the institutional framework when evaluating ESG disclosures. Regulatory agencies in emerging markets should be stricter in verifying ESG disclosures issued by narcissistic CEOs, given the greater risk of opportunism. Originality/value This study examines the interplay between CEO narcissism as a psychological trait and ownership structure as a governance mechanism …
venue: Journal of Financial Reporting and Accounting

title: A hybrid CNN-XGBoost-Temporal Fusion Transformer framework for explainable multi-variable hydroclimatic extremes forecasting under CMIP6 climate scenarios
abstract: Hydroclimatic extremes are projected to intensify across monsoon-dependent river basins, yet reliable forecasting remains limited by three persistent gaps: deep learning models rarely integrate spatial and temporal processing in a unified pipeline, almost always target a single variable, and offer limited interpretability. This study introduces CXTF-Net, to the best of our knowledge the first three-stage hybrid framework for explainable, multi-variable, multi-horizon hydroclimatic forecasting. It combines a CNN-BiLSTM encoder for joint spatial-temporal feature extraction, an XGBoost feature-selection gate that reduces 28 candidate predictors to the most informative 12, and a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) decoder that simultaneously produces calibrated probabilistic forecasts of streamflow, the 12-month Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI-12), a compound flood risk index, and basin water deficit. Applied to a 43-year multi-source record (1980–2022) for the Mahanadi River Basin, India, CXTF-Net achieved an NSE of 0.934, a KGE of 0.921, and an RMSE of 18.4 m 3 /s for 1-day-ahead streamflow forecasting, outperforming seven benchmarks including LSTM (NSE = 0.852), Transformer (NSE = 0.889), and CNN-LSTM (NSE = 0.901) at horizons up to 30 days. NSE exceeded 0.79 at the 30-day horizon across all four target variables. SHAP attribution and attention rollout jointly identified SST…

title: Multifunctional TiO₂-modified cement mortar: experimental investigation, machine learning prediction, and life cycle assessment
abstract: Abstract TiO₂-modified cement mortar is a multifunctional construction material that enhances both mechanical performance and environmental remediation. This study investigated the photocatalytic activity, compressive strength, machine learning prediction, and life cycle assessment of cement mortars containing 0–12 wt% TiO₂. Photocatalytic performance was evaluated through the degradation of Reactive Blue 19 (RB19) dye under visible-light irradiation, while SEM, XRD, and FTIR analyses were used for material characterization. Random Forest (RF) and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) models were developed to predict dye removal efficiency and compressive strength. The photocatalytic efficiency increased with TiO₂ content, reaching 87.13% RB19 removal within 60 min at 10 wt% TiO₂. Acidic conditions enhanced dye degradation, whereas higher dye concentrations reduced removal efficiency. Compressive strength increased to 23.4 MPa at 28 days with 6 wt% TiO₂, representing a 12.3% improvement over the control. The microstructural analysis provide qualitative support for the strength improvement observed at 6 wt% TiO₂. XGBoost achieved the highest predictive accuracy, with testing R 2 values of 0.96 for dye removal and 0.92 for compressive strength. LCA identified cement production as the primary environmental hotspot, while TiO₂ mainly contributed to acidification and particulate matte…

title: Comparative analysis of AI models for cost prediction and feature importance in construction
abstract: Purpose The construction industry has always been plagued by a high number of uncertainties; due to this, cost overruns are the most frequent challenge. To address this problem, this study aims to determine how the presence of risk increases the likelihood of cost overruns and to develop a predictive model that can help reduce them. Design/methodology/approach The research focuses on designing and evaluating prediction models based on artificial intelligence (AI), trained on 101 data points. Performances were compared based on root mean square error (RMSE), coefficient of determination (R2) and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE). A user-friendly front-end tool was developed to increase the practicality of the study, enabling users to see instant cost overrun predictions. Feature importance for risk events has been conducted to find out the most contributing risk events for the prediction model. Findings The adaptive neuro fuzzy inference system model outperformed the rest of the AI models with a testing RMSE of 3.4 and an R² of 0.688 and a validation RMSE of 0.35, an R² of 0.96 and an MAPE of 12.5%. Contract-related risk events were found to be most impactful for cost overrun predictions. Originality/value This study showed a comparison between various types of AI models. It also developed a graphical user interface, bridging the gap between AI and industry applications. Als…
venue: Journal of Engineering, Design and Technology

title: Automatic multiple disease prediction approach using optimized convolutional neural network layers
Benchmarking hyperparameter optimization strategies for crop genomic prediction
abstract: Genomic prediction has become an important approach for accelerating crop breeding by using genome-wide marker information to predict complex traits. However, the performance of genomic prediction models is influenced not only by model selection but also by hyperparameter optimization strategies, which have received limited attention in crop genomic prediction studies. Based on four crop datasets, including maize, rice, wheat, and foxtail millet, we evaluated the prediction performance and computational efficiency of six representative genomic prediction models under four hyperparameter optimization strategies. The results showed that the optimal optimization strategy was jointly affected by crop species, target traits, and model types, and no single strategy consistently performed best across all scenarios. Bayesian optimization showed good prediction stability and achieved high prediction accuracy for most traits and models, especially in the rice and wheat datasets. Grid search and random search also showed strong competitiveness in some datasets. In contrast, although halving search reduced computational cost, it showed lower prediction stability in some cases. Our study highlights the important role of hyperparameter optimization in genomic prediction and provides a useful reference for selecting efficient optimization strategies in crop breeding applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Drug-Likeness Prediction: An Intelligent Framework for Chemical Compound Screening
abstract: Drug discovery requires screening large numbers of chemical compounds to identify promising drug candidates. This study proposes an AI-based framework for predicting drug-likeness using molecular descriptors derived from chemical structures. The framework integrates data preprocessing, feature selection, machine learning model development, and performance evaluation using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUROC. An explainability component is also included to identify important molecular properties influencing predictions. The proposed approach can support early-stage compound screening by prioritizing potentially suitable drug candidates and reducing the need for costly experimental analysis
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology

title: Real-Time Moisture Prediction of Potato Slices during Drying Using RNN and GLCM-Based Image Textural Features
A dynamic graph convolutional network with multiscaled attention for traffic prediction
abstract: Purpose Traffic flow prediction is vital for highway road planning and congestion alleviation. Nevertheless, highway traffic forecasting faces difficulties caused by complex spatio-temporal properties. Existing graph-convolution-based prediction approaches cannot sustain stable spatio-temporal consistency for long horizons. They neglect dynamic spatio-temporal correlations, convolution locality and multiresolution long-term dependencies, limiting prediction accuracy. This paper aims to propose attention-based dynamic graph convolutional recurrent neural network (ADGCRNN) for highway traffic flow prediction. Design/methodology/approach This work presents the ADGCRNN. Self-attention integrates three-resolution temporal sequences for feature extraction. Dynamically constructed multidynamic graphs and adaptive weights capture variant traffic properties. A gated kernel focusing on highly correlated nodes is adopted on full graphs to mitigate graph-convolution overfitting. Findings Evaluated on two public data sets, the proposed ADGCRNN outperforms state-of-the-art baseline models. A practical case study based on a real-world web system further validates the practical benefits of this approach for highway-transportation scenarios. Originality/value This model realizes multiresolution temporal fusion via self-attention. It leverages adaptive multidynamic graphs to model time-varying s…
venue: International Journal of Web Information Systems

title: Decoding patients’ voices: how social media reviews reveal the true impact of medical service
Digital transformation in e-government services: exploring the role of public trust, transparency, accountability and citizen satisfaction in real-time service delivery
abstract: Purpose Governments around the world are initiating e-governance services to streamline administrative procedures and improve citizen satisfaction through advanced technology tools. Particularly, local governments facilitate various e-government services, including personal identification for individuals and their dependents, such as education and health certificates, transportation and revenue services. This study aims to understand the citizens’ intention to use e-governance services. Design/methodology/approach This study used a structured questionnaire grounded in the unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) to collect primary data from individuals who actively use e-governance platforms, such as WhatsApp-based platforms. Confirmatory factor analysis and structural equation modelling (SEM) are used to analyse the data. Findings The results obtained show that such constructs as performance expectancy, facilitating conditions, transparency, trust and accountability significantly and positively impact citizens’ satisfaction, while effort expectancy and social influence have a significant negative impact. Behavioral intention is primarily driven by citizens’ satisfaction. Transparency, on the other hand, positively affects behavioral intention directly, while accountability influences both behavioral intention and citizens’ satisfaction. Research limitations/i…
venue: Journal of Science and Technology Policy Management

title: Scars, scripts and service: rituals of belonging
abstract: Purpose Belonging is a fundamental psychological need. The symbolic practices that shape belonging in hospitality work remain underexplored. The objective of this review is to examine how hospitality workers describe the ritualized practices that facilitate their sense of occupational belonging. Design/methodology/approach This synthesis included peer-reviewed qualitative studies published in English that focused on occupational belonging, socialization, or ritual practices among hospitality workers. A comprehensive search of relevant databases was conducted between October 2024 and January 2025. Data were extracted and synthesized using a meta-aggregative approach to develop categories based on similarity of meaning, which were then aggregated into synthesized findings using the Joanna Briggs Institute SUMARI (Munn et al., 2019). Findings Seven studies met inclusion criteria for the review; 61 findings were extracted, critically appraised and aggregated into 12 categories, which were then synthesized into four overarching findings. The synthesized findings identified belonging in hospitality as a conditional and socially mediated process, constructed through occupational transformation, performances of dominance and subversion, collective functioning and the attainment of recognition and symbolic capital. Practical implications This synthesis offers hospitality-specific recomm…
venue: Journal of Hospitality and Tourism Horizons

title: SS-31 Attenuates Lipopolysaccharide-Induced Injury in HK-2 Renal Tubular Epithelial Cells via SIRT3-Mediated Regulation of Mitochondrial Metabolism
abstract: Background: The mitochondrial-targeting peptide Elamipretide (SS-31) has shown protective effects against sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (S-AKI). Therefore, we investigated the mechanism underlying its effects on lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced injury in renal tubular epithelial cells, with a focus on mitochondrial lipid metabolism and the SIRT3-CPT2 signaling pathway.Methods: Human renal proximal tubular epithelial (HK-2) cells were pretreated with different concentrations of SS-31, followed by exposure to LPS to establish an in vitro model of LPS-induced renal tubular injury. Cell viability and inflammatory cytokine levels were quantified by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Oxidative stress was determined through quantification of reactive oxygen species (ROS), malondialdehyde (MDA), and antioxidant enzyme activities. Mitochondrial membrane potential was detected using JC-1 staining, while intracellular lipid accumulation was assessed with BODIPY 493/503 staining. Fatty acid oxidation (FAO)-associated mitochondrial respiration was analyzed using a Seahorse XF Analyzer. Cell apoptosis was quantified by flow cytometry, and SIRT3 and CPT2 protein expressions were determined by Western blotting. Short hairpin RNA-mediated SIRT3 knockdown was performed to verify the mechanistic role of SIRT3.Results: SS-31 increased L…

title: The Institute of Registration as a Means of Public Legal Regulation of Entrepreneurial Activity
abstract: The article analyzes the approaches formed in the scientific literature to the functional purpose of the institute of registration and its role in regulating the entrepreneurship. The administrative and procedural nature of the registration institution is revealed, the author’s approach to differentiating the material and procedural forms of registration based on the functional purpose of registration is formulated, and the practical significance of such differentiation from the point of view of ensuring the rights of entrepreneurs as participants in the registration relations is argued. The functions reflecting the role of the registration institute as a means of public legal regu-lation of entrepreneurial activity are disclosed. It is shown that the distinction between material and procedural forms of registration has no only theoretical significance, but also practical one, as it allows, in one respect, to focus more attention on the detailed regulation of registration in a procedural form (which can be expressed in the specification of the procedural rights and freedoms of an entrepreneur as a participant in the administrative process, the establishment of additional procedural guarantees such as the possibility of appealing the interim procedural acts in the cases of administrative violation), and at the same time, to orient the public administra-tion system towards the ma…

title: Clinical Evaluation of Bacterial Lysate for Immune Regulation and Exacerbation Reduction in Stable Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
abstract: Background: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide and is accompanied by systemic immune dysfunction, and recurrent acute exacerbations are the main determinants of disease progression, hospitalisation and poor prognosis. Oral bacterial lysates stimulate mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue and have been reported to reduce respiratory infections and exacerbations, but evidence on their immunomodulatory effect in patients with stable COPD is still limited. This single-centre retrospective cohort study, based on clinical data collected during routine care, was designed to investigate whether bacterial lysate Broncho-Vaxom (OM85-BV) can reduce the frequency of acute exacerbations in patients with stable COPD by regulating immune function.Methods: 102 patients with stable COPD admitted to outpatient and inpatient departments were included between January 2025 and October 2025. Based on the treatment methods, they were classified into a control group (CG, basic treatment) and an OM85-BV group (basic treatment combined with oral bacterial lysate). Propensity score matching (PSM) was performed at a ratio of 1:1 using the nearest-neighbour method with a caliper of 0.100. In addition, healthy individuals of the same age group who underwent physical examination in The Fourth People’s Hospital of Lin’an District during the same pe…

title: A New Perspective on the Regulation of Microglia-Mediated Inflammation in Diabetic Retinopathy: Mechanisms of NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation and Therapeutic Strategies
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is among the most common complications of diabetes mellitus and is characterized by microangiopathy and neurodegeneration. Microglia constitute a resident immune population in the central nervous system (CNS) and play crucial roles in regulating retinal angiogenesis under both physiological and pathological conditions. Microglia become widely activated in DR and induce pathogenic angiogenesis by regulating the status of endothelial cells. Modulating the state of microglial activation to ameliorate neovascularization thus appears to be a promising therapeutic approach for managing DR. The NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome is a cytosolic multimeric complex that plays a significant role in innate immunity. After sensing injury, the NLRP3 inflammasome induces the secretion of inflammatory cytokines (including interleukin (IL)-1β and IL-18) and triggers a form of inflammatory cell death known as pyroptosis. Recently, the NLRP3 inflammasome has been found to be abundantly expressed in microglia and has been shown to play critical roles in diabetes-associated neuroinflammation. Here, we summarize the effects of diabetes on NLRP3 inflammasome activity and microglial activation. The regulatory mechanisms of NLRP3, as well as NLRP3-targeted therapeutic strategies in microglia, will be reviewed. Targeting the NLRP3 inflammasome axis might serve as …

title: Reciprocal public AI governance: public AI dividend infrastructure (PAIDI) for public return, data agency and redress
abstract: Purpose This paper aims to address a reciprocity gap in public artificial intelligence (AI) governance: existing frameworks increasingly classify, document and audit AI systems but say less about how governments can make AI-enabled transformation visibly reciprocal through public return, low-burden citizen agency and credible redress. Design/methodology/approach The study develops a conceptual framework through problem-driven theory synthesis. It uses purposive conceptual sampling across AI risk governance, legitimacy, procedural justice, administrative burden, data governance, digital public infrastructure, market concentration and redress and explains how these literatures are combined. Findings This paper theorises public AI dividend infrastructure (PAIDI) as a meso-level architecture linking three layers: public return, citizen agency and assurance/redress. It derives these layers from distributive legibility, actionable agency and remedial credibility deficits. Research limitations/implications This paper is conceptual and offers propositions for empirical and comparative testing. Practical implications The framework identifies policy levers in registries, procurement, interoperability, reporting, assisted agency and claims administration. Originality/value The contribution is architectural rather than component-wise. PAIDI differs from risk-based AI governance, digital pu…

title: Validity of the complete frequency redistribution limit for modeling scattering polarization in the photospheric Sr I 4607 Å line
abstract: Scattering polarization in the line has become a key diagnostic tool for the small-scale unresolved magnetic fields in the quiet solar photosphere, which are inaccessible to Zeeman-based techniques. The limit of complete frequency redistribution (CRD) is commonly used to model the line signals, but its validity and impact on the magnetic sensitivity of this line have not yet been systematically investigated. The proposed study is timely, given the advent of new facilities capable of observing this line with unprecedented accuracy, and of future synoptic programs targeting long-term variations in the quiet-Sun magnetism. We aim to systematically assess the CRD limit against the general partial frequency redistribution (PRD) description of scattering processes for modeling the scattering polarization, focusing on its magnetic sensitivity through the Hanle effect. We solved the radiative transfer (RT) problem for polarized radiation out of local thermodynamic equilibrium (non-LTE) in a semi-empirical 1D plane-parallel static atmosphere, considering both the CRD and PRD scattering descriptions, across a range of magnetic field configurations relevant for Hanle diagnostics. In the presence of small-scale unresolved magnetic fields, where the magnetic field manifests only through Hanle depolarization of the Q/I signal, we found no significant differences between the CRD and PRD emerg…

title: Performance regulation of porous vegetation ecological concrete using carbonated recycled coarse aggregate and fly ash-silica fume blends
abstract: Pores, microcracks, and alkaline calcium-bearing phases in the adhered old mortar of recycled coarse aggregate (RCA) limit its application in porous vegetation ecological concrete (PVEC). To simultaneously satisfy PVEC requirements for load-bearing performance, connected porosity, and reduced alkalinity, this study combined gaseous accelerated carbonation of RCA with the addition of the fly ash-silica fume (FA-SF) blend. The effects of parent concrete strength, RCA carbonation duration, and the FA-SF replacement ratio on the compressive strength, connected porosity, and leachate pH of PVEC were investigated. The evolution of calcium-bearing phases and the aggregate-paste interfacial transition zone (ITZ) was analyzed using thermogravimetric and derivative thermogravimetric (TG/DTG) analysis, X-ray diffraction (XRD), and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (SEM-EDS). The results showed that, as the strength grade of the parent concrete increased from C30 to C50, the compressive strength of recycled-coarse-aggregate porous vegetation ecological concrete (R-PVEC) increased from 3.96 MPa to 5.15 MPa, whereas the leachate pH increased from 12.14 to 12.62. When RCA derived from C40 concrete was carbonated for 5 days at 20 °C, 70% relative humidity, and a CO 2 concentration of 20%, the compressive strength of carbonated recycled coarse aggreg…

title: Down-regulation of miR-23a-3p protects retinal pigment epithelial cells from oxidative stress via inducing SRC-3-mediated autophagy
YAP/TAZ in vascular homeostasis and disease: context-dependent regulation and therapeutic opportunities
abstract: Vascular homeostasis depends on coordinated responses among endothelial cells, vascular smooth muscle cells, and perivascular cells. The Hippo pathway effectors Yes-associated protein (YAP) and transcriptional coactivator with PDZ-binding motif (TAZ) integrate mechanical, metabolic, and biochemical cues within these cell types. Their effects are highly context-dependent, supporting vascular development and integrity under physiological conditions while promoting inflammation, maladaptive remodeling, or calcification in specific disease settings. This review synthesizes the regulatory networks that control YAP/TAZ across vascular cell types and examines their roles in atherosclerosis, angiogenesis, vascular calcification, and related disorders. We further assess emerging YAP/TAZ-directed therapies and define the central translational challenge: achieving cell-, site-, and stage-specific modulation without disrupting essential homeostatic and regenerative functions.

title: Phenolic Profile and Antioxidant Capacity of White Myrtle (Myrtus communis L.) Fruits
abstract: Myrtle (Myrtus communis L.) is a valuable wild fruit native to the Mediterranean ecosystem, increasingly recognized for the bioactivity of its distinct white and dark purple-black morphotypes. This study aimed to comprehensively evaluate the phenolic profile and antioxidant capacities of 70% methanolic extracts derived from white myrtle fruits harvested in the Mersin province. Initial physicochemical analysis determined a moisture content of 72.35±0.05%. Quantitative biochemical assays revealed a total phenolic content (TPC) of 178.28±0.33 mg GAE/100 g fresh weight (FW) and a total flavonoid content (TFC) of 50.62±1.34 mg QE/100 g FW. The extracts exhibited robust antioxidant properties, demonstrating a ferric reducing antioxidant power (FRAP) of 2247.60±89.20 µmol 〖"FeSO" 〗_4⋅7"H" _2 "O" /100 g FW and a DPPH radical scavenging activity (SC_50) of 1.62±0.02 mg/mL. HPLC-PDA chromatographic evaluation identified gallic acid (1034.41 µg/100 g FW) as the major phenolic constituent, with subsequent quantification demonstrating the presence of rutin (207.06 µg/100 g FW), myricetin (135.66 µg/100 g FW), pinocembrin (97.59 µg/100 g FW), quercetin (64.92 µg/100 g FW), and chrysin (61.06 µg/100 g FW). These findings highlight that white myrtle fruits are a rich source of bioactive compounds, demonstrating strong potential as a value-added functional ingredient for the food and pharmaceut…

title: Climate change vulnerability, ecological resilience, and adaptive capacity of Angami agroecological systems in Kohima, Nagland, Northeast India
The Region-Integrator as a Mechanism of International Integration within a Regional Civilization: The Potential of the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia)
abstract: The article examines the problem of subjectivity of international integration within the framework of regional civilizations in the context of the formation of a multipolar world order. It is noted that the existing theories of international integration mainly consider states and international organizations as the main participants in inte-gration processes, paying insufficient attention to the role of subnational actors. In this regard, the author’s con-cept of an integrator region is proposed as an entity capable of initiating and supporting international humani-tarian cooperation within the framework of a regional civilization. The theoretical provisions of the article are tested on the example of the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia), analyzed in the context of the Altai civilization. It is proved that the expressed civilizational identity makes it possible to consider the Republic of Sakha (Yakutia) as an integrator region of the Altai civilization. It is concluded that the proposed concept expands the theoretical understanding of the subjects of international integration and can be used to study the mechanisms of institu-tionalization of regional civilizations in modern international relations.

title: Separation of Methanol and MTBE Azeotrope via Choline-Based Deep Eutectic Solvents: Liquid–Liquid Equilibrium and Molecular Mechanism
abstract: Abstract Methyl tert-butyl ether (MTBE) is an excellent additive for gasoline. Because of the formation of an azeotropic mixture by MTBE and methanol during its production, it is a challenge to separate the azeotrope. To investigate the effect of hydrogen bond donor (HBD) functional groups on extraction performance, three choline chloride-based deep eutectic solvents (DESs) were prepared using ethylene glycol, ethanolamine and glycolic acid, which contain –OH, –NH2, and –COOH, respectively. For separating the azeotropic mixture MTBE and methanol by an extraction process, liquid–liquid equilibrium (LLE) data for the pseudoternary mixtures MTBE + methanol + DESs were ascertained at 298.15 K. Distribution coefficient (D) and selectivity (S) were derived and compared among the different systems. The optimal DES ChCl:MEA attained a distribution coefficient of 8.85 and a selectivity of 436.21. The NRTL model was employed to regress the LLE data. The reliability of the binary parameters of the thermodynamic model was validated through Gibbs energy topology analysis. In addition, quantum chemical calculations and molecular dynamics simulations were applied to investigate the interactions underlying the differences in extractant performance. This multiscale analysis revealed hydrogen bonding Cl···OH plays a crucial function, while van der Waals interactions serve as a secondary contribu…

title: Building multi-stable structures based on Baranov truss part III: limit point (dead-centre) detection in linkage mechanism and non-rigid motion paths computation
abstract: Abstract Part I established a bilateration-based framework for programmable multi-stability in Baranov trusses, showing how discrete geometric configurations can be transformed into stable equilibria through elasticity. Part II extended this foundation into a general design toolkit, enabling scalable multi-stable assemblies through multiple non-rigid links, tessellation and higher-order trusses. In this final part, we extend the framework from trusses to planar linkage mechanisms. Limit-point configurations, classically regarded as dead-centre or singularity states, are here reinterpreted as the gateways between rigid compatibility paths and non-rigid deformation paths. Classical approaches to locating limit points in linkages often rely on Jacobian matrix analysis, which, while rigorous, can be computationally intensive and opaque in interpretation. Here, we present an alternative based on Assur group decomposition and bilateration geometry. Within this framework, a limit point is the rank loss of the active, driver-conditioned bilateration closure Jacobian of the receiving Assur group; this criterion reduces to the collapse of an oriented area for a dyad block and to rank loss of the differentiated closure Jacobian for a tetrad block. This provides a direct, scalable criterion for detecting limit points in one-degree-of-freedom linkages. Two detailed case studies are provided…
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A Mathematical Physical and Engineering Science
